118+    let t ← elabTerm t none
119+    let ty ← whnf (← inferType t)

121+    let st ← elabTerm st none
122+    match_expr ty with
123+    | String => mkAppM ``_root_.MyGetElem.getElem #[st, t]
124+    | Aexp => mkAppM ``Aexp.eval #[st, t]
125+    | Bexp => mkAppM ``Bexp.eval #[st, t]
126+    | _ =>
127+      match ty with
128+      | .forallE _ domain body _ =>
129+        if body.isProp && (← isDefEq domain (mkConst ``_root_.State)) then
130+          pure <| mkApp t st
131+        else
132+          pure t
133+      | _ => pure t

352359 --  A *Hoare triple* is a claim about the state before and
353360 --  after executing a command. A commond notation for Hoare
354361 --  triples, and the one we use in this book, is
355-
356---    {{P}} c {{Q}}
357-
362+--
363+--      {{P}} c {{Q}}
364+--
358365 --  meaning:
359-
366+--
360367 --  - If command `c` begins execution in a state satisfying
361368 --    assertion `P`,
362-
369+--
363370 --  - and if `c` eventually terminates in some final state,
364-
371+--
365372 --  - then that final state will satisfy the assertion `Q`.
366-
373+--
367374 --  Assertion `P` is called the *precondition* of the
368375 --  triple, and `Q` is the *postcondition*.

244+  | `($_ $a $b) => `(aexp { $(getAexp a) - $(getAexp b) })

254+-/

256+  withSourceInfoOf (canonical := false) stx <| Unhygienic.run do

259+    | _ => `(imp_bexp| ~$stx)

261+/--
262+Delaborator for `Bexp.bool`. This is needed since we want to be sure we are
263+matching on the actual `true`/`false` expressions, rather than matching on the
264+delaborated identifiers `true`/`false` (which might not be accurate).
265+-/
266+@[app_delab Bexp.bool]
267+private def BExp.delabBool : Delab := whenPPOption getPPNotation do
268+  let e ← getExpr
269+  guard <| e.isAppOfArity ``Bexp.bool 1
270+  match_expr e.appArg! with
271+  | true => `(bexp { $(mkIdent `true):ident })
272+  | false => `(bexp { $(mkIdent `false):ident })
273+  | _ => failure

284+  | _ => throw ()

288+  | `($_ $a $b) => `(bexp { $(getAexp a):imp_aexp ≤ $(getAexp b):imp_aexp })

291+@[app_unexpander Bexp.gt]
292+private def Bexp.unexpandGt : Unexpander

296+@[app_unexpander Bexp.not]

349+  -- is silent: an unqualified name inside the restatement that should
350+  -- resolve through the enclosing namespace instead falls through to a
351+  -- same-named root declaration, if one exists (e.g. `Nat` resolving to
352+  -- `_root_.Nat` instead of the local shadowing type). Converting the
353+  -- fresh id to a single `Name.str` component keeps it collision-free
354+  -- (its rendered form still can't be written in source) while keeping the
355+  -- namespace chain walkable, and `renameBack`/the constructor comparison
356+  -- only rely on structural prefix matching, which is unaffected.
357+  let ns := Name.mkStr1 (← liftCoreM (mkFreshId : CoreM Name)).toString
